corrections.reason: The prompt requests an interface idea, and the answer conditionally identifies isolated signal transfer plus level adaptation. It does not claim a digital isolator alone transfers every possible sensor format. Accept the architecture concept; implementation still depends on sensor signal type, isolation ratings and isolated-side power. This is not a circuit-ready universal prescription.

Accept the requested one-line motivation that reference noise contributes measurement/output noise. The original does not specify a unit-gain or input-independent transfer function. Actual contribution is input- and topology-dependent and can vanish for ideal zero/ratiometric input; this is qualitative noise-budget guidance, not a universal transfer law.

records.rationale: Correct conduction-loss explanation and conditional thermal consequences for an SSR. It distinguishes mechanical wear advantages from semiconductor temperature limits and says often need heatsinking/derating rather than giving an unsupported universal heatsink or current rating.

evidence.title: OMRON SSR thermal design
evidence.finding: SSR conduction heating equals on-state voltage drop times current, and heatsink thermal resistance must suit the application.
Instantaneous conduction power is v(t)*i(t); an on-state drop of 1.5 V at 10 A gives 15 W to reject. Temperature rise depends on the complete thermal path.

records.rationale: Correct applied-to-rated stress-ratio definition. The fractional limits are illustrative and explicitly depend on component class; they are not presented as the applicable design limits for a selected part or one identified standard.

evidence.title: KEMET tantalum/polymer derating guidance
evidence.finding: Derating reduces applied stress, but recommended voltage limits depend on capacitor technology, series and temperature.

evidence.title: KEMET technology-dependent derating review
evidence.finding: Describes historical 50-percent voltage derating practice for solid tantalum and distinct limits for other technologies; no universal ratio follows.

evidence.title: NASA EEE-INST-002 microcircuit derating
evidence.finding: Section M3 Table 4, PDF page 201, gives a 0.75 power-dissipation derating factor for linear microcircuits; an example, not a universal part limit.
Applied 5 V divided by a 10 V rating gives voltage stress ratio 0.5. Applied and rated quantities must be the same dimension and applicable condition.

records.rationale: The maximum-safe-interruption concept is correct, but without arcing is ambiguous and literally too strong. A fuse commonly forms an internal arc after melting and must extinguish it safely; breaking capacity is not a promise of zero arc formation. Hold the definition pending distinction from unsafe external or sustained arcing.

evidence.title: Littelfuse technical application guide
evidence.finding: Interrupting rating is the available fault current the fuse can interrupt safely at its rated voltage and specified test conditions.

evidence.title: Littelfuse POWR-SPEED technical applications guide
evidence.finding: Section 9 distinguishes pre-arcing and arcing phases; safe fuse interruption does not mean zero internal arc formation.

records.rationale: Correct distinction and interaction between reducing noise generation and controlling coupling/return/bonding paths. It treats source, path, mode conversion and radiation as separate diagnostic links rather than prescribing a single grounding cure.

evidence.title: Analog Devices grounding guidance
evidence.finding: Local bypassing and controlled low-impedance current paths help keep switching currents from contaminating ADC circuitry; topology and frequency matter.

evidence.title: Analog Devices Ferrite Beads Demystified
evidence.finding: Frequency/DC-bias-dependent bead impedance and unwanted LC resonance can worsen power-rail behavior unless damping and application conditions are considered.
Reducing switched di/dt or dv/dt can lower excitation; lowering shared/path impedance reduces noise voltage for a given current. Both effects can interact in a real circuit.

records.rationale: Reasonable diagnostic caution: a software change can alter duty, timing, thermal stress or reported faults without a newly introduced intrinsic hardware defect. The answer says may/could and does not prove the hardware is sound or dismiss actual hardware damage triggered by the new conditions.

evidence.finding: Software timing can change switching frequency and conduction duty, changing average loss and temperature while the physical BOM stays identical.

records.rationale: Correct instruction to account for switching overshoot and actual peak drain stress rather than nominal supply alone. The 24/40/60 V values are illustrative and may be tight is conditional, not a conclusion that every 60 V part is unsuitable for that rail.

evidence.title: Infineon MOSFET linear-mode SOA
evidence.finding: MOSFET electrothermal instability depends on operating point, current temperature coefficient and heat removal; fully enhanced positive on-resistance behavior differs from vulnerable linear operation.

evidence.title: Infineon IRLML6402 datasheet
evidence.finding: Separate threshold, on-resistance and transconductance entries have different gate/drain/current test conditions.

evidence.title: TI MOSFET ringing and voltage margin
evidence.finding: Pages 1–2 explain parasitic LC switching ringing and peak drain-voltage stress.
Parasitic inductive voltage L*di/dt and LC ringing can raise drain voltage above the DC rail; margin requires a bound on the actual peak and operating conditions.

records.rationale: Correctly separates immediate quoted cost from resilience factors and preserves both possibilities for the cheaper choice. No supplier facts, probabilities or purchase decision are invented.

records.rationale: Correctly distinguishes oversampling a slow signal from restoring unavailable sensor dynamics and qualifies the noise benefit as applying to certain kinds of noise. It does not promise that merely raising the read rate improves the sensor's physical bandwidth.

evidence.title: Analog Devices ADC input noise
evidence.finding: Oversampling/noise statistics can improve effective resolution under suitable conditions; quantization and input noise are distinct.
With independent zero-mean sample noise, averaging N readings reduces standard deviation by sqrt(N); correlated noise or absent sensor bandwidth do not gain that same benefit automatically.

The original does not specify a unit-gain or input-independent transfer function. evidence.title: Analog Devices reference noise effect
evidence.finding: Reference noise produces signal-dependent conversion error; the ideal reference contribution vanishes for shorted zero input and grows toward full scale.

evidence.title: Analog Devices ADC spur analysis
evidence.finding: Reference-input noise can feed through into ADC codes, motivating reference-noise control at the relevant operating point.
For code=K*Vin/Vref, a small reference perturbation gives delta_code≈-K*Vin*deltaVref/Vref². This is not a fixed additive output term independent of input.
